31.0.s.en: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

31.0.0.en: Moses began to speak to the people in a farewell address about the matters mentioned in the following verses up to (v. 6). He reminds the people that he has become an old man advanced in years, having reached one hundred and twenty, and that he is no longer able to lead the people as he did throughout the past forty years, from the time he worked to bring them out of Egypt until now. Moreover, the Lord had told him to transfer the leadership to another, for he would not cross the Jordan with his people into the Promised Land.

31.1.0.en: Moses reassures them that after his death the Lord will not leave them alone, for He will cross the river before them, represented by the ark of His covenant, which represents the presence of the Lord, and they will defeat the peoples who stand in their way. The Lord will destroy those peoples and give His people their land. Nor will the Lord leave them without a leader to lead them after his death, the death of Moses, for He had already appointed for them Joshua the son of Nun, the disciple of Moses, to lead them.

31.2.0.en: Just as the Lord gave them victory over Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, drove them out of their lands and gave their lands as a possession to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, He is able to do the same to the other peoples dwelling in the Promised Land, driving them out and giving His people possession in their place.

31.3.0.en: When the victory over those peoples is achieved for them, they must deal with them as He had commanded them on more than one occasion, namely, that they destroy those peoples, tear down their altars and remove their traces, so that they would not afterward be influenced by their pagan worship.

31.4.0.en: Moses encourages them not to fear the might of the enemies, because God will walk in their midst and go before them, and will not forsake them or leave them alone to face the enemy.

31.5.0.en: Here Moses transfers the task of leading the people, as the Lord commanded him, to his disciple Joshua the son of Nun.

31.5.1.en: He calls him to take up the leadership before all the people, so that everyone may know that he is the new leader and that they must walk behind him. Moses urges him to be ready to bear the responsibility and to arm himself with courage, for he is the person charged by the Lord to enter with his people into the Promised Land, as He had promised their fathers to give them that land, and it is for him to divide the land among the tribes.

31.6.0.en: Moses reassures his disciple Joshua that he will not be alone in carrying out those tasks, for the Lord will lead him in his journey and accompany him in all his steps; He will take care of him and will not forsake him, so he should fear nothing and dread no enemy.

31.6.1.en: God chose Joshua to lead the people after Moses for the following reasons:

31.6.2.en: 1- He was the special disciple who clung to Moses and learned from him more than all the others.

31.6.3.en: 2- He went up alone with Moses on the mountain and remained forty days waiting for Moses until he returned with the commandments (Ex 24:13).

31.6.4.en: 3- He and Caleb alone, out of all twelve spies, reassured the people and strengthened their faith to enter the Promised Land, but they refused (Num 14:6, 7).

31.6.5.en: 4- He used to stand at the door of the tent of meeting when Moses left it, until he returned to it; this was the tent that preceded the tent that held the ark (Ex 33:11).

31.6.6.en: 5- He led the war against Amalek and was victorious through the prayers of Moses.

31.6.7.en: If you receive a responsibility, do not be afraid, for God is with you. Ask for His help and go forward courageously toward the responsibility you are fulfilling, and He will complete His work in you.

31.7.s.en: (2) The reading of the Torah at the Feast of Tabernacles

31.7.0.en: The Torah: a word meaning law, and it is the first five books of the books of the Old Testament, which Moses wrote under the guidance of the Lord. He completed it on that last occasion and then delivered it to the priests and the elders of the people, as those entrusted with keeping it, teaching it to the people and handing it down to the following generations. The priests are described as the bearers of the ark of the covenant because they were charged with the affairs of the ark, so they carried it, in place of the Kohathites (Num 4:6, 15) (the Levites of the clan of Kohath), on special occasions, such as what happened when the people crossed the Jordan behind the new leader Joshua the son of Nun (Josh 3:3).

31.8.0.en: The Feast of Tabernacles: the third of the great principal feasts, in which the people must dwell in booths that they build in open places or on the roofs of houses, to remember their dwelling (they or their fathers) in tents throughout their journey in the wilderness of Sinai (Num 29:12-38). The year of release: every seventh year, also called the sabbath of the land because the land is not plowed in it. In it the creditor had to forgive his debt, and the Hebrew slave was set free. Moses commanded them to read this Law in the hearing of all the people when they gather in the year of release at the Feast of Tabernacles, in the place of the celebration, which is the holy place where the house of the Lord is established, such as Jerusalem (Lev 25:2).

31.9.0.en: All the people, men and women, children and elders, Hebrews and resident strangers, had to come in the seventh year, the year of release, at the Feast of Tabernacles, to the place of the house of the Lord. The presence of the children here was by divine wisdom, that they might see the rites of the feast and hear the texts of the Law, so that this glorious picture would be fixed in their minds and remain engraved in their thoughts, and when they grew up and became men they would take over carrying them out and hand the tradition down to the following generations.

31.9.1.en: For this reason the Church of the New Testament is careful to urge fathers to bring their children, while they are still in childhood, to attend her blessed rites and to enjoy her Holy Sacraments, so that they grow up holding fast to her teachings and her doctrines take root in their souls.

31.10.0.en: The sons of the following generations among them, who did not live through the Lord's glorious works with His people, hear the word of the Lord and learn from it His will and desire for their lives. So they live in His fear all the days that they remain in the land to which they are crossing the Jordan to settle in it.

31.11.0.en: Once again the Lord announces to Moses that his earthly life is about to end, and asks him to summon Joshua to the tent of meeting so that both of them may present themselves before the Lord, for the Lord often met with the people at the door of the tent of meeting, where He appeared in a pillar of cloud. So Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he and Joshua stood to receive what the Lord wanted to charge them with.

31.12.0.en: The glory of the Lord appeared in the pillar of cloud, which stood at the door of the tent. For God announces His presence among His people, the transfer of leadership from Moses to Joshua, and the encouragement of Joshua to carry out his new responsibility.

31.13.1.en: The Lord announces to Moses anew that he will depart from the world and sleep as his fathers slept before him, having performed his mission in the best way. And the Lord declares to him, according to His foreknowledge of events, that the stubborn, fickle people will forsake their true God and betray His covenant with Him by going to worship gods strange to them, the gods of the peoples around them, after they dwell in the Promised Land.

31.14.0.en: Because my God is not in my midst...?: the people ask, could the cause of my misfortunes be that God has left me?

31.14.1.en: God's anger will be kindled against them in those days in which they will commit immorality, and He will leave them as they left Him and no longer look upon them with mercy, for they have lost their worthiness of His care and protection. Their enemies will humble them, and misfortunes and afflictions will come upon them until they repent, confess their sins, and know that what has befallen them is because the Lord has left them and no longer dwells in their midst because of their worship of idols.

31.14.2.en: Do not lose God's care for you and all His love for the sake of any passing desire or evil pleasure, for the love and care of God are more important than anything. And do not be lax about a small sin, lest it lead you to a greater one and God forsake you.

31.15.s.en: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

31.15.0.en: The Lord commanded Moses to write a song whose details He would inspire him with, as it is recorded in the next chapter. He must teach it to the people, explain its details to them, and make them learn it so that it becomes fixed in their minds. The song contains comparisons between the Lord's great work with them and how they meet it with betrayal of His covenant.

31.15.1.en: Thus there are two means of strengthening the people's faith:

31.15.4.en: Praising God strengthens your faith in Him and increases your love for Him. So take care to praise God as part of your prayers at home and also in the Church.

31.16.0.en: The Lord foretells to His people what will happen from them after they enter the Promised Land, which He promised their fathers and which overflows with many good things. Instead of thanking the Lord for His abundant kindnesses, which provided them with fullness and wealth, luxury and comfortable living make them forget the source of all good, who is God, abundant in mercies, so they break His covenant and worship other gods.

31.17.0.en: When afflictions come upon the people and they repeat this song to which they are accustomed, they will remember that the cause of the afflictions is their distance from God. For God foretells them their coming evils so that they may guard against them and not do them.

31.18.0.en: Moses obeyed the Lord's command to him, so he wrote the song and taught it to the children of Israel at the end of his life on earth, and it is what is written in (ch. 32).

31.19.0.en: Then the Lord's charge to Joshua the son of Nun was to be strong in resolve and courageous in his leadership of his people to fight the enemies, assuring him that it is He who will lead His people and bring them into the Promised Land which He swore to their fathers to give them, and He also assured him that He will not leave him alone but will be with him and support him in his mission.

31.20.s.en: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

31.20.0.en: When Moses finished writing the five books of the Torah, including the song mentioned, he commanded the priests of the tribe of Levi to take the copy of the Torah that he had written and put it beside the ark of the covenant, to declare the Lord's kindnesses to His people, His warnings to them, and the punishments awaiting them if they betray His covenant. They used to put it in a special chest beside the ark, in addition to other copies of the Torah that the priests kept to read to the people.

31.21.0.en: For I have lived through the recklessness of your conduct toward the Lord and your repeated rebellion against Him. This happened despite my being among you and my attempt to teach you, guide you and care for you; how much worse will it be after my departure from this world?

31.22.1.en: Therefore he asked them to have all their elders gather to him, the heads of the tribes and the distinguished elite among them, so that he might recite to them the words of the song inspired to him by the Lord, that they might be responsible thereafter for instructing it and teaching it to the following generations of the people. And all living creatures, heavenly and earthly, and all of nature would be witnesses to the Lord's works with them and to their ingratitude and disobedience.

31.23.0.en: For Moses knows what evils the people will commit in the future, as the Lord had already told him, and also from his previous experience with them. Therefore punishment comes upon them in the following generations.

31.24.0.en: The congregation of Israel: includes the heads, the elders and the officers.

31.24.1.en: The elders gathered to him as the representatives and leaders of the people, and he recited in their hearing the words of the song in full, as a faithful teacher and trustworthy messenger who conveys faithfully what God wanted to say to His people.

31.24.2.en: Be committed to presenting God's word to all those around you, even if they will be affected by it only temporarily and may neglect it afterward, for perhaps you will win some of them, and your words will be a rebuke to the rest when they fall into sin and afflictions come upon them.

32.0.0.en: Here Moses the prophet draws the attention of his hearers, the people of Israel, to the fact that the words they are about to hear are the word of the Lord, inspired to him to convey to his people. And these words are the song in which Moses calls heaven and earth, that is, all living creatures, to be witnesses against this people, to declare the justice of God in regard to the people's conduct if they violate the covenant.

32.1.0.en: A figurative description of the teachings of the Lord that Moses conveyed to the people, which are described as follows: Drop as the rain: as the rain falls on the earth and waters its plants, the teachings of the Lord come down to His people and water their spirits and develop their spirituality.

32.1.1.en: And distil as the dew: as the dew refreshes nature, those teachings refresh souls.

32.1.2.en: As the small rain upon the tender herb: as the rain is a watering of the grass on which the cattle graze, the teaching of the Lord is a watering of souls.

32.1.3.en: And as the showers upon the grass: as the heavy rain gives life to the herbs and makes them grow, so the word of the Lord gives life to souls and waters hearts.

32.2.0.en: Moses the prophet says that when he utters the song, he is calling upon the name of the person of the Lord and proclaiming the greatness of His glory and the generosity of His kindnesses.

32.3.0.en: He likens the Lord to a rock as the firm foundation on which His people rest, and "his work is perfect" means that His works are perfect, without lack or defect. All His dealings with human beings are just, and He remains faithful to His covenant and wrongs no one. He is righteous and free from every error, and gives each one according to his deeds, whether by reward or punishment, without injustice.

32.3.1.en: Would that you praised God every day in your prayers and glorified Him for all His works. This gives you reassurance and joy, and even shows on your face, so that you are cheerful and make others glad.

32.4.s.en: (2) A rebuke of the people for disobedience

32.4.0.en: He prophesies of the sin of the children of Israel against the Lord and the corruption they will commit before Him, so that they no longer deserve to be called the sons of God or His own because of their blemishes and the deficiencies of their deeds, for they are a crooked generation, greatly perverse and fickle.

32.5.0.en: In a tone of reproach Moses faults them for meeting the Lord's kindnesses to them with such ingratitude and corruption. By this they showed a lack of understanding and wisdom, whereas it would have been better for them to think of the rights of His fatherhood over them, for He is their Creator and it is He who formed them into a chosen people apart from the other peoples.

32.5.1.en: Remember God's kindnesses to you, so that you are ashamed of your sins and turn away from them, and try to draw near to good works as a return of thanks for God's love and care for you.

32.6.s.en: (3) The Lord's work with His people

32.6.0.en: Thy father: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, or their father according to the flesh.

32.6.1.en: Moses urges the people to turn their memory back to the past and remember what the Lord provided His people of care and kindness over many generations, from the calling of their father Abraham, then Isaac and Jacob. And the young among them, who did not live in the time of God's leading of them by the hand of Moses in bringing them out of Egypt and His care for them in the wilderness of Sinai, should ask their fathers and the elders of the people, who were children in Egypt and lived through those events, to tell them what happened before of God's care for them, so that they increase in faith and trust in the Lord.

32.6.2.en: This is what our Church does, for she often takes us back to the lives of the saints and the sayings of the Fathers so that we increase in knowledge of the history of our Church and our martyrs, and the children's knowledge of the lives of their fathers grows, so that their faith is strengthened and they remain firm in the pure and correct teaching. So take care to read the history of the Church and the lives of the saints, and ask their intercessions so that they may accompany you in your life and you live strong and reassured.

32.7.0.en: The text here speaks of the Promised Land, in that God had placed in His eternal plan that this piece of earth would be the portion of the children of Israel. From the time humanity was scattered over the earth, there were borders for every region inhabited by one of the peoples, and this holy land was inhabited by the Canaanites before the iniquity of these peoples was full, so that the Lord took it from them and gave it to His people at the time appointed in His divine purpose. So this land was the portion allotted by God to His people from of old.

32.7.1.en: In his saying "he set the bounds of the people" according to the number of the children of Israel (the sons of Jacob), he means the Canaanite peoples who inhabited the land of Palestine before it was taken from them and given to the sons of Jacob. The number of those peoples was twelve, the same as the number of the sons of Jacob and the tribes of Israel (Gen 10:15-18).

32.8.1.en: The lot of his inheritance: the boundaries of the share, the boundaries of the inheritance, since in ancient times they used to measure the land with a cord of known length.

32.8.2.en: God's portion is His children, and the children's portion is the Lord. So the song says that the Lord's portion is His people (Ps 16:5), meaning that the people of Israel are a people special to the Lord among all the peoples who divided the earth among themselves and were scattered in various directions, since it is the people who knew the true God above all other peoples.

32.9.0.en: He speaks of God's care for His people in the wilderness of Sinai, a land in which life is difficult for lack of water or food, so God shepherded them, preserved them, fed them and cared for them as one cares for the most important thing in his body, which is his eyes.

32.10.0.en: His wings: the shoulder, and its muscles are among the strongest muscles of the body.

32.10.1.en: Here he likens God's care and tending of His people to what the eagle does for her young, for she flutters over them as a figure of her care for them, and spreads her wings to fly with them, carrying them on her shoulders to teach them to fly.

32.11.0.en: Thus the Lord did with His people, for He led them and cared for them with no strange god sharing in it. He took them by the hand so that they passed over the mountains of Sinai on their way in the wilderness, and He gave them to eat of the fruits that they found on their way, and of the wild honey that they came upon in the desert, and of the oil that they took from the olive trees that grow in rocky places.

32.12.0.en: Then when they entered the Promised Land they enjoyed its abundant good things. There was butter and milk from the produce of their many cattle, and they ate their flesh and fat, and they possessed the lands of Bashan, of which Og was king (ch. 3), which are lands rich in rams and sheep because of the abundance of their pastures. Likewise the wheat from which the finest kinds of flour are made is from the produce of the fertile lands in which they live, and they used to make wine from the fruit of the vines that flourish in the lands of Canaan, and the Lord blessed it as He blessed all its agricultural crops.

32.12.1.en: Reflect on God's care for you throughout your past life, and you will find wonderful works you did not expect. So thank God for them, that your enjoyment of what is in your hand now may increase and God's blessings to you may grow.

32.13.1.en: Jeshurun: a name given to the people of Israel, meaning the beloved.

32.13.2.en: Here he likens Israel to an unruly animal that the shepherd tended with the best care and fed with the best food until it grew fat from much eating, and instead of obeying its shepherd, it rejected him. Instead of thanking God for the abundance of His kindnesses, Israel rejected grace and loved disobedience, and left the Lord who had made of it a distinguished people and enfolded it with His care and blessing, and its eyes were blinded to the truth that God is its refuge, who saved it in the past and saves it in the present and the future, and this is the utmost folly on the part of the people of God. These are prophecies of what the children of Israel will do, and he will continue them in the following verses.

32.14.0.en: The Lord is jealous for His glory and for His people who worship other gods alongside their worship of Him, gods whom their fathers did not know, for they are strange to them. And they angered the Lord by their betrayal of Him and of His covenant. The expression that God was jealous and angry are human figures that bring the spiritual meaning near to the mind, and never mean that God is moved as human beings are moved, but mean the Lord's displeasure with the deeds and conduct of His people.

32.15.1.en: The people offered sacrifices to gods who are not God, gods newly known to them, whose works they had never experienced before, as they had experienced God's works with them, and whom their fathers did not heed but rather despised.

32.16.0.en: He returns to liken the Lord to a rock, that is, that He is almighty and unchanging. It is He who formed them into a people and brought them out into the light and made them a strong people, feared by the peoples around them. But sadly the people forgot that it was God who formed them into a great people and brought it into being out of nothing and made it a great nation after it had been a small, weak company.

32.16.1.en: Know that every sin you commit is rebellion against God, and it is never right to meet God's kindnesses by committing these sins. So repent quickly, for He is merciful and receives you, and you regain your sonship and your glories.

32.17.s.en: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

32.17.0.en: Moses the prophet continues his prophecies and announces that the Lord's decision, based on what happened of the people's betrayal of His covenant, is to neglect them and not look upon them.

32.18.0.en: And the Lord said, I will no more shepherd them or care what happens to them, but I will look at what will come upon them of afflictions as a result of their deeds. They are not firm in their faith but are unfaithful, treacherous children who have forgotten God's love for them.

32.19.0.en: They have stirred up My anger by their worship of false gods, idols made by the hands of men, so I too will stir up their jealousy and wrath. And God has indeed allowed ignorant pagan nations to trouble and persecute them, such as the nation of the Babylonians. These foreign nations signify the faith of the Gentiles in Christ at the time when many of the Jews refused to believe in Him (Jn 1:11, 12).

32.20.0.en: Their evil works kindle the fire of divine wrath, which burns even to the depths of hell, as if it extends from the surface of the earth to reach the depth of hell, so that the land on which they live becomes as though it were part of hell because of the dread of the torments to which they will be subjected. And in its extension from the surface of the earth it comes upon the fields and their crops and destroys the mountains from their foundations above their heads.

32.21.0.en: The Lord sets afflictions and woes upon them, and they attack them like many armies, and He also aims His blows at them so that misfortunes strike them.

32.22.0.en: The poison of serpents of the earth: the venom of reptiles.

32.22.1.en: For since they are exhausted by intense hunger resulting from the ruin of the land, and wearied by the burning fever and deadly diseases that have struck them, and have no strength at all to resist, God sets upon them the wild beasts that devour them with their fangs, and the poisonous reptiles that sting them with their venom.

32.23.0.en: Bereaves: makes mothers lose their children.

32.23.1.en: Chambers: plural of chamber, the private room of the bridegroom and his bride.

32.23.2.en: If they appear outside their homes, the armies of the enemies kill them, so that their mothers are bereaved, and if they hide inside the houses, they are in trembling and fear. All are subject to this, whether young man or young woman, nursing infant or aged man.

32.24.0.en: God decided in His anger to scatter His people among the peoples of the world, as happened in the days of the Assyrian or Babylonian kingdom, until the name of His people almost disappeared among the peoples of the earth.

32.25.0.en: Here too fear and provocation are figurative expressions, for God does not fear and is not provoked, but what is meant is His anticipation of what the enemies of the children of Israel will say, if the Lord actually decides to carry out His plan of destroying them and blotting out their memory, for the enemies would claim that they were the ones who did that by their own power, and not that what happened was by the Lord's permission and will, since He used them as an instrument of discipline for His people. So in keeping His holy name, God did not blot out His people completely but disciplined them severely, and then, when they repented, brought them back to their land, that is, returned them from captivity.

32.25.1.en: If God allows you a trial, examine yourself lest it be because of your sins, and know that your God is merciful and wants your repentance, not your destruction. So return to Him by repentance, and He will remove the afflictions from you and you will enjoy His blessings.

32.26.s.en: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

32.26.0.en: He continues his prophecies in these verses and shows that the nation of Israel will become devoid of understanding and discernment, as their shameful conduct proves. They are lacking in insight because they do not think of the consequence of what they do.

32.27.0.en: If they were wise they would think much before committing those evil deeds, and would compare their state while enjoying the promises of God if they choose the way of life with their falling into the woes of which the Lord warned them many times if they disobeyed Him.

32.28.0.en: Just as he showed what weakness the people of God will reach when they forsake Him (ch. 28:1, 7, 15, 18), so here he affirms the same meaning, announcing that one soldier of the enemies' soldiers will chase a thousand of them, and two will put ten thousand to flight, which means that victory or defeat is not by the strength of armies but by the will and pleasure of the Lord and by what accomplishes His divine plan. A defeat like this cannot be understood except that God was angry with them and in His anger delivered them to their enemies because they did not keep His covenant.

32.29.0.en: Our mighty God is not like the weak gods of the enemies, and this is what the enemies themselves admit, even if the enemies sit as judges in the comparison between our strength and theirs.

32.30.0.en: Here, in an eloquent simile, he mentions the evil deeds of Israel for which God delivers them to their enemies, saying:

32.30.1.en: Their vine is of the vine of Sodom: the vine is a grapevine whose fruits are bad, like Sodom, which committed many evils.

32.30.2.en: And of the fields of Gomorrah: here he likens the badness of the deeds of the children of Israel (that is, the fruit of their works) to vineyards, that is, grapevines that give bad fruit, like the wicked deeds of Gomorrah.

32.30.3.en: Their grapes are grapes of poison, their clusters are bitter: their fruit is deadly poison and all their deeds are shameful deeds that make whoever contemplates them feel intense bitterness.

32.30.4.en: The subject of vineyards and grapes here reminds us of what is in (Isa 5:1, 2), which means that the vineyard the Lord planted (which is the people of Israel), from which the Lord expected good grapes, yielded bad grapes.

32.30.5.en: Their wine is the poison of serpents and the deadly venom of asps: asps is the plural of asp, which is a snake, and the poison of serpents means the venom of serpents.

32.30.6.en: These peoples offer deadly poison, like the venom of serpents and snakes, instead of good wine.

32.30.7.en: If you care to be a disciple of the word of God and the teachings of the Church, you gain wisdom, understanding and guidance in all your steps in life, and you keep away from the toil of the world around you, immersed in desires that lead it to destruction.

32.31.s.en: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

32.31.0.en: God gathers the fruits of the evil deeds of the children of Israel and puts them in His treasuries until the proper time for punishment, when He repays them for their errors and takes vengeance on them.

32.31.1.en: Here God likens the sins of the children of Israel, and likewise of the other peoples, to what a person keeps and stores in his treasuries and seals up. And God forgives them if the person repents, and repays for them if the person persists in his evil.

32.32.0.en: God is the Avenger of the wicked and repays them justly for what they have committed. The Lord may delay sending punishment to give an opportunity for repentance, but the punishment is near, for it is known and decreed in His divine plan. Let not the wicked think that the Lord's delay means that He has overlooked their evils; rather He is patient with the sinner, hoping that this forbearance will lead him to repentance, but God at the same time prepares the retribution and carries out the punishment at the proper time.

32.33.0.en: And though the Lord judges His people if they sin, He has compassion on them and has mercy on them if they repent and return to Him, and when He sees that their strength has weakened from the severity and dread of the blows and chastisements that came upon them, which struck everyone and from which neither free nor slave was exempted.

32.34.0.en: God mocks the false gods that His people followed and relied upon, saying, where are they now that they are in this condition, and why did they not hasten to protect them and help them? The children of Israel used to offer sacrifices to them and pour out drink offerings, imagining that they eat and drink, when they are nothing but idols.

32.35.0.en: The Lord tells them that it is He who punished them and He alone is able to deliver them, and no one shares divinity with Him. He has all authority to give life and to put to death. If He crushed them because of their evils in fulfillment of justice, He is also the Merciful One, able to heal them and deliver them from the lowliness and crushing in which they are.

32.36.0.en: Lifting the hand to heaven: a gesture that indicates an oath, or an announcement of the disclosure of divine truths to human beings.

32.36.1.en: God declares and affirms that He is the only God and lives forever, and is not like the false gods and idols that neither move nor feel.

32.37.0.en: My glittering sword: the shining sword.

32.37.1.en: My hand take hold on judgment: I have set myself up for judgment.

32.37.2.en: I whet my sword: I have made my sword sharp and ready to kill.

32.37.3.en: When the Lord decides to take vengeance on the peoples who were excessive in their cruelty to His people when God used them as a rod of discipline, He pictures Himself as a horseman preparing to enter a battle, whetting His shining sword to bring those peoples to judgment, taking vengeance on them and repaying them for what they did to His people and for their gloating over them, and also punishing them for all their evils, for they hated the Lord and worshiped idols.

32.38.0.en: Here are wonderful similes by which the Lord depicts His vengeance on His enemies. His arrows with which He will strike the enemy will shed much blood, so that these arrows become as if drunk from having drunk so much of their blood. And His sword devours the flesh of the enemies, so the sword is covered with the blood of the enemies who will be killed, in addition to others who will be taken captive. The sword of the Lord will also cut off the heads of the enemy commanders, boasting in their strength.

32.39.0.en: Rejoice, O Gentiles, His people: St. Paul quoted it in (Rom 15:10) from the Septuagint, "Rejoice, O Gentiles, His people." This is a reference to the Gentiles being made partakers with the people of God in the salvation in Christ, and rejoicing in the fulfillment of this wonderful salvation, for it is a prophecy of the salvation in Christ and the entry of the Gentiles into the faith.

32.39.1.en: And taking the text in its direct meaning, the writer of the song here calls the nations of the world to rejoice and praise the God of Israel, who avenges the blood of His people, returns vengeance upon His enemies, and is merciful to His land and to His people.

32.39.2.en: God defends you if you obey His commandments and always return to Him by repentance. And even if He allows disciplines for you and wrongs from others, be confident that they are temporary and that He will give you victory and glorify you in the end.

32.40.0.en: Moses declared the words of this song to the people and repeated it before them many times, that they might repeat it after him and memorize its words and its melodies. And Joshua the son of Nun helped him in having the people memorize it, because he was the leader next after him.

32.41.0.en: Moses charged them to teach this song to their children and have them memorize it, because it alerts them to keep the Law of God and to worship Him. This song bears witness against whoever memorizes it of the necessity of following God and encourages him in that.

32.42.0.en: Moses told them that the words of this song are not merely a tune or idle talk, but are the core of their life, establishing them in the upright life and ensuring them stability in the new land, the land of Canaan, so that no enemy crowds them in it.

32.42.1.en: Take care to memorize the Psalms and repeat them, not only at the appointed time of prayer but throughout the day, for they guard your thoughts and guide you in your words and conduct, so that you always live pure before God.

32.43.s.en: (9) Moses sees the land of Canaan but does not enter it

32.43.0.en: This mount Abarim, mount Nebo: Mount Nebo is one of the chain of the mountains of Abarim, and its highest peak is the top of Pisgah (ch. 3:27). This mountain lies in the land of Moab east of the Jordan, opposite the city of Jericho, which lies west of the river (Map 6, 8). With Moses' having the people memorize the song, his service came to an end, so God commanded him to go up to the highest peaks of mount Abarim to see the Promised Land that God had promised His people, and then die rejoicing at having completed his service and the fulfillment of God's promises.

32.44.0.en: God announced to Moses that he would die on this mountain and that God would hide his body, lest the children of Israel worship it because of their great love for him. Thus ends the life of Moses, the chief of the prophets, and he dies like the rest of human beings and like his brother Aaron, who died and was buried on mount Hor (Num 20:28).

32.45.0.en: So that Moses might remain humble before God until the end of his life, He reminded him that he had sinned when he and Aaron doubted God's word, for instead of commanding the rock at Meribah to bring forth water, he struck it twice (Num 20.) But Moses' being deprived of entering the Promised Land because of this sin is not a belittling of Moses' greatness; rather, it represents a stage in the leadership of the people, since he had reached an advanced age, so that after him his disciple Joshua would begin a new stage, namely, entering the Promised Land.

32.45.1.en: It is good for us to follow the example of Moses the prophet and accept willingly any divine discipline that our Lord allows for us, accepting it without complaint or rebellion, and entrust our lives to Him with faith and thanksgiving, knowing that His merciful, loving hand will have compassion on us and will enter our lives to bring us out of affliction into light, for all that happens in our lives is part of His comprehensive divine plan for us and the fulfillment of His will in our existence.

32.45.2.en: The blessing of Moses upon the children of Israel
